slot.title: Matched grip and the full stroke
slot.lessonGoal: Hold the sticks in matched grip and play a relaxed full stroke that rebounds to its starting height.
objectives: Hold a drumstick in matched grip, with the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger
Describe a full stroke: the stick starts high, strikes the head, and rebounds to its starting height
Explain why letting the stick rebound keeps the hands relaxed

visuals.intent: A hand holding a drumstick in matched grip, seen so the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger is plain, for the Learner to copy.
The four moments of a full stroke in order, raised, striking, rebounding, and back at the starting height, so the Learner sees the stick come back up on its own.

lesson.title: Matched grip and the full stroke
lesson.lessonGoal: Hold the sticks in matched grip and play a relaxed full stroke that rebounds to its starting height.
objectives: Hold a drumstick in matched grip, with the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger
Describe a full stroke: the stick starts high, strikes the head, and rebounds to its starting height
Explain why letting the stick rebound is compatible with keeping the hands relaxed

blocks.text: Imagine a stick in each hand, both held the same way: matched grip. For your playing, the aim is a relaxed hold and a stick that bounces back naturally after a hit [1]. The fulcrum, the point the stick turns around, lies between your thumb and index finger [2]. In matched grip, your thumb runs along the stick opposite the index finger’s first knuckle at the fulcrum, and your other fingers wrap loosely around the stick [2].

blocks.caption: A hand holds a drumstick with the palm down, the thumb along the stick, and the other fingers loosely curled.
blocks.alt: A hand seen from above at a slight angle, with the palm facing down, the thumb running along the drumstick, and the other fingers loosely curled around it.

descriptor.caption: Matched grip in both hands: each stick is pinched between the pad of the thumb and the first joint of the index finger, with the remaining fingers curled loosely around it.
descriptor.alt: Close-up of two hands side by side holding drumsticks from above, thumbs along the sticks and index fingers hooked under them.

blocks.text: A full stroke is a hit that starts with the stick high and finishes at the same height [2][3]. Your wrist raises the stick; the stick then drops to the drum, strikes its surface, and bounces back up [2][1]. The full stroke has no stopping point on its way down or back up [1].

blocks.caption: The Course’s own schematic shows a full stroke returning to its starting height.
blocks.alt: Four panels labelled Start high, Strike, Bounce up, and Back at starting height show a raised stick, its tip touching the drum, an upward arrow beside the rising stick, and the stick back at its original height and angle.

descriptor.caption: The Course’s own schematic shows a full stroke returning to its starting height.
descriptor.alt: Four panels labelled Start high, Strike, Bounce up, and Back at starting height show a raised stick, its tip touching the drum, an upward arrow beside the rising stick, and the stick back at its original height and angle.

sections.heading: The bounce and the relaxed hand

blocks.text: The drum supplies energy for the stick’s return, and your hand allows that bounce rather than stopping it [4]. Your thumb and index finger stay in contact with the stick while your wrist and fingers stay relaxed [1]. A full stroke combines a relaxed hold with a return to the stick’s starting height [2][1].

glossary.definition: A way of holding drumsticks with both hands using the same hand position.
The point around which an object turns.
A drum hit in which the stick starts high and returns to the same height.

brief.subject: A four-panel schematic of a drumstick moving from a raised position to the drum and back to its starting height.
mustShow: Exactly four panels run from left to right, labelled Start high, Strike, Bounce up, and Back at starting height.
The first panel shows the stick raised with its tip pointing upward.
The second panel shows the stick tip touching the drum surface.
The third panel shows the stick rising away from the drum, with an upward arrow.
The fourth panel shows the stick at the same height and angle as in the first panel.
brief.caption: The Course’s own schematic shows a full stroke returning to its starting height.
brief.alt: Four panels labelled Start high, Strike, Bounce up, and Back at starting height show a raised stick, its tip touching the drum, an upward arrow beside the rising stick, and the stick back at its original height and angle.

proposed.definition: A way of holding drumsticks with both hands using the same hand position.
The point around which an object turns.
A drum hit in which the stick starts high and returns to the same height.
